title: Bind a browser spec to every human-facing train

facts.note: Trains are declared under plan/; the rule reports at the train's plan file. No layer classification is required.
Needs the htmx_e2e_detector to parse train declarations for a `user:` participant and match them against `// Train:` bindings in browser specs.

Any test file, regardless of filename, whose header comments carry `// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…` or `// URN: test:journey:…` counts as a browser spec; needs a header-comment scanner.

fires: A train is added or changed under plan/ with a `user:` participant and no browser spec carries `// Train: <train id>`.
The only file mentioning the train is a unit test that holds the journey URN in a string.
A browser spec bound to a train is deleted or its `// Train:` header is removed, leaving the train uncovered.
doesNotFire: A train whose participants are only wagons and systems (no person takes part).
Files inside node_modules, dist, build or _generated trees.
A human-facing train already bound by at least one browser spec via `// Train:`, including a misnamed test file whose header carries a journey marker.

given: A human-facing train (one with a `user:` participant) is declared under `plan/`.
when: The tester writes or reviews browser coverage for declared trains.
then: Ensure at least one browser spec is bound to that train by a `// Train: <train id>` header.
prefer: Add `e2e/<train-slug>.e2e.ts` with `// Train: <train id>`, then make it prove the train, not merely name it.
Claim: read the declared train/journey behavior; identify the user-observable outcome it should deliver.
Stimulus: enter through the declared user-facing entrypoint; perform the real browser interactions that exercise the train.
Witness: assert the final user-visible business outcome, not only navigation, a 200 response, or an internal state token.
avoid: Adding the Train header solely for coverage credit.
Calling an internal handler instead of walking the assembled journey.
Asserting only that the page loaded while the train behavior stays unobserved.
Counting a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string as a browser spec.
Treating structural coverage as proof: a spec that only binds the train, navigates successfully, or mentions its identifier can pass coverage while the journey behavior stays unproven.
unless: Trains in which no person takes part (only wagons and systems) have no screen to drive and are out of scope.
why: A train with no browser spec is a silent gap: its journey can regress with nothing turning red. `// Train:` is only the coverage handle, not the proof — binding, navigating, or naming the train satisfies coverage yet leaves behavior unproven.
evidence: Every train under plan/ with a `user:` participant has at least one browser spec whose header carries `// Train: <train id>`.
A meaningful bound spec starts from the declared user-facing entrypoint, performs the interactions that make the train relevant, and asserts the user-observable business outcome the journey promises.
Verify: the spec would turn red if the train's user-facing behavior regressed.
verifier_detail: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not one.
Human-facing train = a train declared under `plan/` in which a `user:` participant takes part; trains with only wagons and systems are skipped.
Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
The rule reports at the train's plan file, where the gap was declared.

The `// Train:` binding is the detector's coverage handle, not the proof itself: a spec that only binds the train, navigates successfully, or mentions its identifier can satisfy structural coverage while leaving the journey behavior unproven (judge quality by review).
audit: Statement: Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.train-e2e-coverage`, strict (metadata.mirrors: tester.vite.train-e2e-coverage).
summary: Every declared train has a browser spec.

splitSuggestion.then: A browser spec bound to a train must enter through the declared user-facing entrypoint, perform the real interactions of the train, and assert the user-visible business outcome so it turns red if the journey regresses.

additions.text: The source carries two obligations: (1) every human-facing train has a bound browser spec (kept in `then`), and (2) the bound spec meaningfully proves the journey (Claim/Stimulus/Witness/Avoid/Verify). (2) is kept in prefer/avoid/evidence here and proposed as separate convention tester.htmx.train-spec-proves-journey.
additions.justification: One obligation per `then`; the quality obligation is not detectable by the same structural detector.

additions.text: Fires/doesNotFire example situations (e.g. spec deletion leaving a train uncovered) are derived from the statement and exceptions.
additions.justification: Required activation examples; they restate source scope and add no new obligation.

additions.justification: Losslessness across readers wins over brevity (auditor required S015 in coder-facing fields).
